passages.provision_quote: Is a citizen of the United States and has provided SATISFACTORY evidence of CITIZENSHIP as PRESCRIBED in section 16-166
passages.note: Chaptered House Engrossed text of HB 2492 makes evidence of citizenship a qualification to register and directs recorders to reject registration applications not accompanied by it.
Overview page shows HB 2492 was signed as Chapter 99 and lists sponsors without Pingerelli, so her act on this bill is a vote, not sponsorship; the page itself prints no operative clause.
House Third Reading final passage with 26 members voting No, so the vote is not near-unanimous, and the Arizona House is the same chamber of the same legislature as her current seat.

rows.reasoning: Pingerelli voted "PINGERELLI Y" on House Third Reading of HB 2492 (2022), a single-subject registration and citizenship bill that passed the Arizona House "Passed 31-26-3-0-0". Its chaptered text qualifies a resident to register only if the resident "Is a citizen of the United States and has provided SATISFACTORY evidence of CITIZENSHIP as PRESCRIBED in section 16-166", and directs the recorder to "reject any application for registration that is not accompanied by satisfactory evidence of citizenship", which is the rung requiring documentary proof of citizenship to register to vote. The weaker proof-of-location-of-residence clause beside it does not set the chair.
